target_customer: Global software and AI companies, billing and commerce platforms and accounting firms that need cross-border sales tax, VAT and GST compliance
problem: Companies selling across borders must register, calculate, file and remit indirect tax in many jurisdictions, and legacy vendors rely on manual research and partners.
business_model: B2B SaaS and managed compliance for indirect tax, pricing not public
product_category: AI native cross-border tax compliance platform

founders.name: Nicholas Rudder
founders.background_notes: YC page says he is from Sydney and worked at PwC and Macquarie in TMT finance, and that he ran a B2C marketplace that exposed him to indirect tax problems. Education not found.

founders.name: Adrian Sarstedt
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2025-11-18) names him as co-founder and says he is no longer at the company. Background not found.

competitors.name: Maven
competitors.what: Cohort based course platform where creators attract their own audience, compared with ScholarSite which builds instructor sites and handles distribution and payments

technical_complexity.rationale: At the YC batch Sphere was ScholarSite, an educational marketplace with standard web, payments and scheduling engineering. The later tax engine (TRAM, direct connections to 130 plus authorities) is much harder, rated 4, but came after 2023.

defensibility.rationale: A course marketplace was easy to copy at the batch. The later direct authority integrations and tax engine add a stronger moat that did not exist at founding.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The edtech marketplace was being shut down; after the pivot, rivals Anrok, Avalara and Fonoa competed in tax while Stripe offered tax calculation but is treated by the CEO as a partner.

market_need_then: The marketplace had enough traction to raise a 4.3 million seed, but its tax liability on gross merchandise value is what the founder says exposed the tax compliance need that became the later product. Direct demand evidence for the tax product at founding is not applicable.

branding.name_origin: Rudder kept the ScholarSite name, then rebuilt the business as Sphere after the pivot. TechCrunch gives no meaning for the word Sphere.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct pitch to founders: it should not be your job to understand 190 tax systems

branding.brand_signature: It shouldn't be your job to understand 190 tax systems

rebrands.why: Pivot from an educational marketplace to tax compliance software, per TechCrunch. The exact rename date is not stated, 2023 is the stated launch year of Sphere as a tax vendor.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic common word shared with many products, though named customers like Lovable and Replit give credibility. No brand press found.

pivots.from: ScholarSite, an educational marketplace for professional courses
pivots.why: The founders were preparing to shut ScholarSite down; Rudder kept the company and built tax software after marketplace tax compliance problems, per TechCrunch.

outcome_analysis: Sphere entered YC as an edtech marketplace, nearly shut down, and then rebuilt itself in 2023 as a cross-border tax compliance vendor serving fast growing AI companies. After about two years in stealth it announced a 21 million Series A led by a16z in 2025-11. The pivot drew on the CEO's own marketplace tax pain, and competition from Anrok, Avalara and Fonoa remains intense.
notes: Seed conflicts: TechCrunch says 4.3 million; ZoomInfo dates it 2022 with Uncommon Capital and Y Combinator, another source says Felicis led; one aggregator says a 6 million seed. Investors are partly from aggregators. Anrok raised a 4.3 million seed in 2021-06 and Fonoa raised 25 million in 2021-11 for tax automation, but those rivals relate to the later tax product, not the edtech company at the batch. The edtech competitor list rests on one undated post. ScholarSite appears in a 2021-12 Poets and Quants list, so the W22 company was ScholarSite.
